name: Cybercrime — Online Romance Scam (Estafa via Electronic Means)
citation: RA 10175 §6 in relation to RPC Art. 315
fullText: Romance and investment scams conducted on social media or dating apps are prosecuted as estafa committed through information and communications technology, with the penalty one degree higher than ordinary estafa under RA 10175 §6. Victims should preserve chat logs, transaction receipts, wallet addresses, and bank/GCash records. PNP-Anti-Cybercrime Group (ACG) and NBI-CCD accept walk-in complaints and online reports via cybercrime.gov.ph.
keywords: romance scam, investment scam, online dating fraud, swindling, estafa, Facebook, Telegram, GCash

name: Cybercrime — Online Sextortion and Sexual Exploitation
fullText: Threatening to publish nude or sexual images of a person unless they pay or perform sexual acts is criminalized under the Anti-OSAEC Act (RA 11930) if a child is involved (life imprisonment) and the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act (RA 9995) when an adult is involved (3-7 years and ₱100k-₱500k fine). Victims should not pay, preserve screenshots, block the account, and report to PNP-WCPC, ACG, or NBI-CCD.
keywords: sextortion, nude photo blackmail, OSAEC, voyeurism, revenge porn, private photo, minor exploitation

name: Cybercrime — Cyber Libel via Facebook or Social Media
fullText: Cyber libel is libel committed through a computer system. Under RA 10175 §4(c)(4) the penalty is one degree higher than ordinary libel (RPC Art. 355). Each repost or boost can be treated as a separate publication. Truth is a defense only if published with good motives. Prescriptive period is 15 years (Tolentino v. People). Preserve URL, post ID, timestamps, and witness accounts who saw the post.
keywords: cyber libel, online defamation, Facebook post, Twitter, social media, reputation, online insult

name: Online Lending App Harassment and Doxxing
citation: RA 10173 + RA 9474 + SEC Memorandum Circular No. 18-2019
fullText: Unfair debt collection practices by online lending apps (contact-shaming, threats, sending defamatory texts to your contacts, doxxing) violate the Data Privacy Act (RA 10173), the Financing Company Act (RA 9474), and SEC MC 18-2019. The borrower may file a complaint with the National Privacy Commission (NPC) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Maintain screenshots of harassing messages and the app's privacy policy at install time.
keywords: online lending, predatory lending, contact shaming, NPC, SEC, debt harassment, doxxing, loan shark

name: Phishing and Account Takeover (GCash, Maya, Bank)
fullText: Phishing, smishing, and SIM-swap attacks resulting in withdrawals from GCash, Maya, or bank accounts are prosecuted under RA 10175 (computer-related fraud) and RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulation Act). Victims should freeze the affected account immediately, file a dispute with the e-money issuer (BSP-supervised), report to PNP-ACG, and preserve SMS and email logs.
keywords: phishing, smishing, account takeover, SIM swap, GCash hack, bank fraud, unauthorized transfer

name: Unauthorized Access (Hacking) of Social Media Account
fullText: Hacking another person's Facebook, Instagram, email, or game account constitutes illegal access under RA 10175 §4(a)(1), penalized with prision mayor or a fine of at least ₱200,000. Victims should change all passwords, enable 2FA, request a platform-side recovery, and report to PNP-ACG with the offender's username/UID if known.
keywords: hacking, account hack, Facebook hack, illegal access, password theft, 2FA, identity theft

name: Online Marketplace Scam (Lazada / Shopee / Facebook Marketplace)
fullText: Sellers who collect payment but never ship — or who ship a wrong, counterfeit, or empty item — commit estafa via electronic means and violate the Consumer Act (RA 7394). Buyers should first file in-platform dispute and chargeback. For amounts ≤ ₱1,000,000, a small-claims action can be filed even without a lawyer. Counterfeit goods may also violate the IP Code (RA 8293).
keywords: online shopping scam, Lazada, Shopee, Facebook marketplace, counterfeit, refund, chargeback, small claims

name: Unauthorized Recording / Streaming of Private Calls
fullText: Recording private phone, Zoom, or Messenger calls without all-party consent violates the Anti-Wiretapping Act (RA 4200), and distributing the recording online may add cyber libel or unjust vexation. Recordings obtained without consent are inadmissible in court. Penalties: 6 months to 6 years imprisonment.
keywords: wiretapping, secret recording, Zoom recording, private call, eavesdropping, inadmissible evidence

name: Catfishing and Identity Theft Online
fullText: Computer-related identity theft (using another person's identifying information online — name, photos, IDs — without consent) is penalized under RA 10175 §4(b)(3) with prision mayor and a fine of at least ₱200,000. Victims can request takedown from the platform under its impersonation policy and file a complaint with PNP-ACG.
keywords: catfishing, identity theft, impersonation, fake profile, deepfake, social engineering

name: Spreading of Disinformation and Fake News
fullText: Publishing false news that endangers public order is penalized under RPC Art. 154 (arresto mayor + fine). Done online, the penalty is elevated under RA 10175. Spreading deepfakes of officials or private persons may also expose the poster to cyber libel.
keywords: fake news, disinformation, deepfake, false report, public order, online hoax

name: E-Commerce Contract Disputes
fullText: Electronic documents and signatures (clicks, OTPs, digital signatures) have the same legal effect as written documents under RA 8792. Contractual disputes about online orders, terms-of-service breaches, or refund obligations are governed by the Civil Code on contracts and may be filed in small claims or regular courts.
keywords: e-commerce, electronic signature, online contract, terms of service, refund, OTP

name: Unwanted Sexual Messages and Online Sexual Harassment
citation: RA 11313 (Safe Spaces Act) — Online Sexual Harassment
fullText: Sending unsolicited sexual images, persistent sexual comments, or stalking through DMs is gender-based online sexual harassment under the Safe Spaces Act (RA 11313). Penalties: arresto menor + ₱100,000-₱500,000 fine for serious cases. Take screenshots before reporting to PNP-WCPC.
keywords: safe spaces, online harassment, unsolicited photo, DM harassment, sexting, RA 11313

name: Bayanihan / Pandemic Online Solicitation Fraud
fullText: Soliciting donations for fake calamity, hospital bills, or charity drives on social media and absconding with the proceeds is estafa committed via ICT. Victims may pool their complaint-affidavits to qualify for syndicated estafa (if 5 or more conspirators).
keywords: online solicitation, fake donation, charity scam, calamity fraud, gofundme scam

name: Job Posting Scam (Recruitment Fraud Online)
fullText: Online job postings demanding upfront 'placement fees' or asking for nude photos or ID copies for fake 'verification' are illegal recruitment and may also constitute estafa or human-trafficking attempt. Verify the recruiter at DMW's POEA license search before paying anything.
keywords: job scam, recruitment fraud, fake job, DMW, POEA, placement fee, illegal recruitment

name: Unauthorized Disclosure of Personal Data (Doxxing)
fullText: Publishing someone's home address, phone number, family details, employer, or financial information without consent and with malicious intent is a Data Privacy Act violation. Penalties: 1-3 years imprisonment + ₱500,000-₱2,000,000 fine. Report to the National Privacy Commission within 72 hours of discovery.
keywords: doxxing, personal data leak, address shared online, NPC, privacy, data exposure

name: Annulment — Psychological Incapacity (Article 36)
citation: Family Code Art. 36 (as construed in Tan-Andal v. Andal, G.R. 196359, May 11 2021)
fullText: Psychological incapacity is now treated as a legal — not strictly medical — concept (Tan-Andal v. Andal). It must be proven by clear and convincing evidence of personality structure that makes a spouse incapable of complying with essential marital obligations. Expert testimony is no longer indispensable. Filed before the Regional Trial Court (Family Court).
keywords: annulment, psychological incapacity, family code, art 36, Tan-Andal, divorce alternative

name: Annulment — Fraud and Lack of Consent
fullText: A marriage may be annulled within five years if fraud induced consent (e.g., concealment of pregnancy by another, STD, drug addiction, conviction for crime involving moral turpitude). Lack of parental consent (party 18-21 at time of marriage) is another ground. Annulment differs from declaration of nullity (no marriage existed in the first place).
keywords: annulment, fraud, concealment, no parental consent, void marriage, nullity

name: Legal Separation Grounds
fullText: Legal separation may be sought for: repeated physical violence; moral pressure to change religion or political affiliation; drug addiction or chronic alcoholism; lesbianism or homosexuality; bigamy; sexual infidelity or perversion; attempt against the life of the spouse; abandonment for more than 1 year; final judgment of imprisonment for more than 6 years. Legal separation does NOT dissolve the marriage bond, but separates the parties' bed, board, and properties.
keywords: legal separation, family code, infidelity, abandonment, drug addiction, art 55

name: Child Custody and Tender-Age Doctrine
fullText: A child under seven (7) years old shall not be separated from the mother unless the court finds compelling reasons (e.g., neglect, abandonment, immorality, habitual drunkenness, drug addiction). For children seven and above, the court considers the child's choice with the paramount standard of the best interest of the child.
keywords: child custody, tender age, mother custody, best interest, family court, parental authority

name: Child Support and Computation
fullText: Both legitimate and illegitimate children are entitled to support proportionate to the giver's means and the child's needs. Support covers sustenance, dwelling, clothing, medical, education, and transportation. Failure to give support without justification may constitute economic abuse under RA 9262 (VAWC). A petition for support pendente lite can be filed simultaneously.
keywords: child support, monthly support, VAWC economic abuse, illegitimate child, support pendente lite

name: Illegitimate Child Surname (RA 9255)
fullText: An illegitimate child may use the surname of the biological father if the father expressly acknowledges paternity through the birth certificate (with thumbmark), affidavit of acknowledgment, or any public document. Without acknowledgment, the child uses the mother's surname. Affidavit to Use the Surname of the Father (AUSF) is filed with PSA.
keywords: illegitimate child, surname, father acknowledgment, RA 9255, AUSF, PSA, birth certificate

name: Adoption — Domestic Administrative Process
fullText: Domestic adoption is now administrative (no court order required) and handled by the National Authority for Child Care (NACC). Filing simplifies and reduces costs. Foreign adoptions remain governed by the Inter-Country Adoption Act. Adopted children gain the same rights as legitimate children for support and inheritance.
keywords: adoption, NACC, RA 11642, foster care, inter-country adoption

name: Abandonment and Withholding Financial Support
fullText: A spouse or parent who deliberately deprives the woman or child of financial support — including denying funds for school, food, or medicine — commits Economic Abuse under VAWC (RA 9262). Penalties: 6 months to 12 years and a fine of ₱100,000-₱300,000. Victim may seek BPO/TPO/PPO for immediate protection and support.
keywords: VAWC, economic abuse, withholding support, abandonment, BPO, financial neglect

name: Recognition of Foreign Divorce (RA 9223 line of cases)
citation: Family Code Art. 26 (2) — Republic v. Manalo, G.R. 221029
fullText: A divorce obtained abroad by either the foreign spouse OR the Filipino spouse (Republic v. Manalo doctrine) may be judicially recognized in the Philippines, freeing the Filipino to remarry. A Petition for Recognition of Foreign Divorce is filed at the RTC where the petitioner resides. Proof of the foreign divorce decree and foreign law is required.
keywords: foreign divorce, recognition, Republic v Manalo, art 26, remarry, RTC petition

name: Conjugal vs Absolute Community Property
fullText: Marriages without a prenup celebrated on or after Aug 3 1988 default to Absolute Community of Property (all assets owned at marriage + acquired during marriage are co-owned). Earlier marriages default to Conjugal Partnership of Gains. Properties acquired by gratuitous title (inheritance, donation) generally remain exclusive.
keywords: absolute community, conjugal property, prenup, property regime, family code

name: Anti-Bigamy Law
fullText: Contracting a second marriage while the first marriage is still subsisting and undissolved is bigamy, punishable by prision mayor. A judicial declaration of nullity is required before the first marriage is legally considered void — even a void marriage cannot be ignored without a court decision.
keywords: bigamy, second marriage, void marriage, art 349, declaration of nullity

name: Anti-Mail Order Spouse Act
fullText: Prohibits arrangements that match Filipino women or men to foreign nationals for marriage or common-law cohabitation as a business. Penalties: 15-20 years imprisonment + ₱500,000-₱2,000,000 fine.
keywords: mail order bride, RA 10906, foreign matching, trafficking

name: Magna Carta of Women
fullText: Comprehensive rights framework: 60-day special leave for surgery related to gynecological disorders, equal access to education, protection from discrimination in the workplace, accommodation for pregnant workers, and women's representation in policy bodies. PCW oversees implementation.
keywords: magna carta women, RA 9710, special leave, gender equality, PCW

name: Parental Authority and Discipline (Anti-Corporal Punishment in the Home)
fullText: Parental discipline that inflicts physical injury, humiliation, or psychological harm crosses into child abuse under RA 7610. DSWD may intervene; in serious cases parental authority can be suspended or terminated by the court. School corporal punishment is also banned under DepEd Child Protection Policy.
keywords: parental discipline, corporal punishment, child abuse, RA 7610, DepEd CPP, physical injury

name: Anti-Bastardization (Rights of Illegitimate Children)
citation: Family Code Art. 176 (as amended) and Art. 887
fullText: Illegitimate children are entitled to support, education, and inherit one-half (½) of the share of legitimate children. Acknowledged illegitimate children also have visitation rights enforceable in family court.
keywords: illegitimate child, inheritance, support, acknowledgment, family code

name: Just Cause vs. Authorized Cause Termination
fullText: Just causes (Art. 297) — serious misconduct, willful disobedience, gross/habitual neglect, fraud or willful breach of trust, commission of crime against employer — require twin-notice and hearing. Authorized causes (Arts. 298-299) — installation of labor-saving devices, redundancy, retrenchment, closure, disease — require 30-day notice to both employee and DOLE, plus separation pay. Failure on substantive OR procedural due process makes dismissal illegal.
keywords: just cause, authorized cause, twin notice, separation pay, illegal dismissal, DOLE

name: Constructive Dismissal
citation: Labor Code jurisprudence (e.g., Globe Telecom v. Florendo-Flores)
fullText: Constructive dismissal occurs when continued employment is rendered impossible, unreasonable, or unlikely due to demotion, discrimination, sustained harassment, or unjustified diminution of pay or rank. The employee is deemed to have been illegally dismissed. Backwages and reinstatement (or separation pay in lieu) apply.
keywords: constructive dismissal, demotion, harassment at work, diminution, backwages, NLRC

name: Regular vs Project / Seasonal / Fixed-Term Employees
fullText: A worker is regular if engaged for activities necessary or desirable to the usual business of the employer, or if a casual worker has rendered ≥ 1 year of service (whether continuous or broken). Project employees are tied to a specific project with defined start/end. Misclassification — labeling regular work as 'project' — can be challenged before the NLRC.
keywords: regular employee, project employee, casual, fixed term, NLRC, art 295, endo

name: Overtime, Night Shift, and Holiday Pay
fullText: Work beyond 8 hours commands overtime pay of 25% (regular day) or 30% (rest day/holiday). Night-shift differential of 10% applies to work between 10 PM and 6 AM. Regular holidays pay 200% if worked; special days pay 130%. Managerial employees and field personnel are typically exempt.
keywords: overtime, night shift, holiday pay, regular holiday, special day, NSD

name: Service Incentive Leave and 13th Month Pay
fullText: Employees with ≥ 1 year of service are entitled to 5 days paid Service Incentive Leave (commutable if unused). 13th month pay (1/12 of basic salary earned in the calendar year) must be paid not later than December 24 of each year, regardless of company performance, under PD 851.
keywords: 13th month pay, PD 851, service incentive leave, SIL, year-end bonus

name: Retirement Pay (RA 7641)
fullText: An employee who reaches 60 (optional) or 65 (compulsory) and has served at least 5 years is entitled to retirement pay equivalent to one-half (½) month salary for every year of service. 'One-half month salary' includes 15 days, 1/12 of 13th month pay, and cash equivalent of 5 days SIL.
keywords: retirement pay, RA 7641, age 60, age 65, retirement age, lump sum

name: Migrant Workers Act (OFW Rights)
fullText: OFWs are protected from illegal recruitment, illegal placement fees, and contract substitution. Migrant Workers Act allows OFWs to file money claims at the NLRC (not POEA arbitration) within 3 years. DMW issues OEC and oversees licensed recruitment agencies. Repatriation in case of war, calamity, or contract violation is the obligation of the recruiter and DMW.
keywords: OFW, migrant worker, RA 8042, DMW, POEA, NLRC, repatriation, contract substitution

name: Sexual Harassment in the Workplace (RA 7877 + Safe Spaces)
fullText: RA 7877 covers quid-pro-quo and authority-based sexual harassment. RA 11313 expands to peer-to-peer harassment, including unwanted sexual remarks and conduct. Employers must form an internal Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI). Failure to act exposes the employer to solidary civil liability.
keywords: workplace sexual harassment, CODI, RA 7877, safe spaces, hostile environment

name: Maternity Leave Extension and Pay (RA 11210)
fullText: 105 days paid maternity leave for live childbirth (cash benefit from SSS based on monthly salary credit, plus salary differential paid by employer for the gap). 60 days for miscarriage. Additional 15 days for solo parents. Up to 7 days transferable to the father or alternate caregiver.
keywords: maternity leave, RA 11210, SSS, 105 days, solo parent, paternity transfer

name: Wage Order — Minimum Wage in Davao Region (RTWPB XI)
citation: RTWPB XI Wage Order No. RB XI-22
fullText: The Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board (RTWPB) Region XI sets the minimum wage for Davao Region. As of the latest order, non-agriculture minimum wage in Davao City is approximately ₱481/day with COLA adjustments. Wage Orders are subject to periodic review. Check the latest order at DOLE-RXI before relying on a fixed amount.
keywords: minimum wage, Davao, RTWPB, wage order, COLA, region XI

name: Single Entry Approach (SEnA) Mandatory Conciliation
fullText: Before filing a formal labor case at the NLRC, both parties must undergo 30 days of mandatory conciliation-mediation at the DOLE Regional Office under the Single Entry Approach. Cases settled at SEnA produce a binding compromise agreement.
keywords: SEnA, DOLE conciliation, mandatory mediation, NLRC, labor dispute

name: BPO and Night Worker Health Standards
fullText: Mandates additional health assessments, fortified meals, transport for late-shift workers, and an 8-hour rest between shifts. Applies to call centers, BPOs, and other night-work establishments.
keywords: BPO, call center, night shift, health, DOLE, transport

name: Foreclosure of Real Estate Mortgage — Right to Redeem
citation: Act No. 3135 (Extrajudicial Foreclosure) + Civil Code Art. 1601
fullText: After extrajudicial foreclosure, the mortgagor may redeem the property within 1 year from registration of the certificate of sale (banking institutions: shorter periods under General Banking Law). Redemption price = bid price + 1% per month interest + taxes. After the redemption period, the buyer consolidates ownership.
keywords: foreclosure, mortgage, redemption, Act 3135, real estate, bank loan

name: Deed of Sale — Documentary Requirements
fullText: A valid deed of sale of real property must be notarized and contain the parties, technical description, consideration, and signatures. Transfer of title requires capital gains tax (6%), DST (1.5%), and transfer tax (0.5%) before the Register of Deeds issues a new TCT. Failure to register exposes the buyer to later sale to a third party in good faith.
keywords: deed of sale, TCT, capital gains tax, transfer tax, Register of Deeds, notarized

name: Co-Ownership and Partition
fullText: Co-ownership exists when ownership of a thing belongs to different persons in undivided shares. Any co-owner may demand partition at any time; the action is imprescriptible. Properties that cannot be physically divided are sold and the proceeds split proportionally.
keywords: co-ownership, partition, undivided share, inheritance, sibling dispute

name: Donation Inter Vivos and Mortis Causa
fullText: Donation of real property must be in a public instrument and accepted by the donee in the same or separate public instrument (Art. 749). Donations mortis causa (taking effect upon death) must comply with formalities of a will, otherwise void. Donor's tax applies under the Tax Code.
keywords: donation, donor tax, public instrument, mortis causa, real property

name: Adverse Possession and Acquisitive Prescription
fullText: Ownership over real property may be acquired by extraordinary prescription after 30 years of uninterrupted, peaceful, public, and adverse possession (10 years if with just title and good faith). Possession of titled (Torrens) land cannot ripen into ownership through prescription.
keywords: adverse possession, prescription, Torrens title, 30 years, ownership

name: Boundary Disputes and Relocation Survey
citation: Civil Code Art. 481 + DENR Survey Regulations
fullText: Owners with disputed boundaries may commission a relocation survey by a licensed Geodetic Engineer based on the technical descriptions in their TCTs. A barangay conciliation is required before filing in court (Katarungang Pambarangay). Misplaced monuments or encroachments may also expose the offender to malicious mischief or qualified theft.
keywords: boundary dispute, relocation survey, geodetic, neighbor, barangay, encroachment

name: Free Patent and Public Land Disposition
fullText: A Filipino citizen who has actually occupied and cultivated agricultural public land for at least 30 years may apply for a Free Patent. Residential Free Patents are governed by RA 10023 (simplified one-time grant for actual occupants of public residential land ≤ 200 sqm).
keywords: free patent, public land, CA 141, RA 10023, DENR, agricultural

name: Right of First Refusal in Sale of Tenanted Land
fullText: Long-term tenants in urban land covered by the Urban Land Reform Act (PD 1517) and beneficiaries under RA 7279 enjoy a right of first refusal when the landowner sells. Failure to honor this right voids the sale and may entitle the tenant to the same purchase price.
keywords: right of first refusal, urban land reform, tenant, PD 1517, RA 7279

name: Subdivision Developer Refund and Cancellation (Maceda Law)
fullText: Buyers of real estate on installment who have paid at least 2 years of installments are entitled to a 50% cash refund (up to 90% with longer years) on cancellation by the developer. Buyers with less than 2 years get a 60-day grace period to settle.
keywords: Maceda Law, RA 6552, real estate refund, subdivision cancellation, installment

name: Statute of Limitations for Crimes (Prescriptive Periods)
fullText: Death/reclusion perpetua: 20 years. Other afflictive penalties: 15 years. Correctional penalties: 10 years (except arresto mayor: 5 years). Light offenses: 2 months. Libel: 1 year (15 years for cyber libel). Prescription begins from discovery and is interrupted by complaint filing.
keywords: prescription, statute of limitations, RPC arts 90, libel, cyber libel

name: Frustrated vs Consummated vs Attempted Crime
fullText: Consummated felonies have all elements present. Frustrated felonies have all acts of execution performed but the crime is not produced for reasons independent of the offender's will. Attempted felonies commence direct overt acts without performing all acts of execution. Penalties decrease by one or two degrees from consummated form.
keywords: consummated, frustrated, attempted, art 6, stages of crime

name: Self-Defense and Justifying Circumstances
fullText: Self-defense requires: (1) unlawful aggression, (2) reasonable necessity of the means employed, (3) lack of sufficient provocation by the defender. Unlawful aggression is the indispensable element — without actual or imminent attack, self-defense fails. Defense of relatives and strangers have parallel requirements.
keywords: self defense, unlawful aggression, art 11, justifying circumstance, defense of relative

name: Plea Bargaining in Drug Cases
fullText: Accused charged with possession of dangerous drugs (RA 9165) may plea-bargain to lesser offenses within fixed thresholds (e.g., possession of < 5g shabu may be downgraded to drug paraphernalia possession under §12). DOJ guidelines (DC No. 27-2022) align prosecutorial discretion. Plea bargaining is not allowed for sale (Sec. 5).
keywords: plea bargain, drugs, RA 9165, A.M. 18-03-16-SC, downgraded, paraphernalia

name: Probation Law
fullText: Probation is available to offenders sentenced to imprisonment of not more than 6 years, on application after judgment becomes final. RA 10707 lets accused who lose on appeal still apply for probation. Excluded: those sentenced to > 6 years, drug pushers, election offenses, those who already enjoyed probation.
keywords: probation, PD 968, RA 10707, 6 years, alternative to imprisonment

name: Bail — Right and Conditions
citation: Constitution Art. III §13 + Rules of Court Rule 114
fullText: All persons in custody are entitled to bail except those charged with offenses punishable by reclusion perpetua when evidence of guilt is strong (capital offense). Bail may be cash, surety, property, or recognizance. Forfeited bail can be reinstated upon production of accused within 30 days.
keywords: bail, recognizance, surety, reclusion perpetua, capital offense, Rule 114

name: Right to Counsel and Custodial Investigation (Miranda)
fullText: Persons under custodial investigation must be informed in a language they understand of: (1) the right to remain silent, (2) the right to counsel preferably of their own choice, (3) the right to have the proceedings reduced in writing in the presence of counsel. Confessions obtained without counsel are inadmissible. Investigating officers face 8-10 years imprisonment for violations.
keywords: Miranda, RA 7438, custodial investigation, right to counsel, inadmissible confession

name: Anti-Hijacking and Aviation Crimes
fullText: Penalizes hijacking, unauthorized carrying of explosives/firearms on a Philippine-registered aircraft, and acts endangering aviation safety. Penalties range up to life imprisonment.
keywords: hijacking, aviation, aircraft, RA 6235, in-flight

name: Anti-Plunder Act
fullText: Public officers who amass ill-gotten wealth of at least ₱50,000,000 through a combination of overt acts (kickbacks, malversation, misappropriation) commit plunder, punishable by reclusion perpetua and perpetual disqualification.
keywords: plunder, RA 7080, ill-gotten wealth, public officer, corruption

name: Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act
fullText: Penalizes 11 corrupt practices of public officers, including causing undue injury to government through manifest partiality, evident bad faith, or gross inexcusable negligence (Sec. 3(e) — most-cited provision). Penalties: 6 years and 1 month to 15 years + perpetual disqualification.
keywords: graft, RA 3019, anti-corruption, public officer, Sec 3(e), undue injury

name: Anti-Sandiganbayan and Ombudsman Jurisdiction
fullText: Sandiganbayan exclusive jurisdiction covers RA 3019, RA 7080, and other crimes by public officers occupying SG 27 or higher (or specifically enumerated). Lower-ranking officials are tried in regular RTC. Ombudsman investigates and prosecutes.
keywords: Sandiganbayan, Ombudsman, SG 27, public officer, RA 8249

name: Anti-Red Tape Act and EODB
citation: RA 11032 (EODB and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act)
fullText: Government agencies must process simple transactions within 3 working days, complex within 7, highly technical within 20. Violations expose officers to fines, suspension, and dismissal. Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) receives complaints.
keywords: ARTA, red tape, RA 11032, EODB, government service, 3-7-20 rule

name: Anti-Truancy and Curfew Ordinances
fullText: Truancy or violation of LGU curfew by a minor is treated under RA 9344. Minors are NOT detained but turned over to parents or DSWD social worker. Curfew violation alone is not a criminal offense unless tied to a more serious act.
keywords: curfew, truancy, minor, juvenile, RA 9344, DSWD

name: Acts of Lasciviousness
fullText: Lascivious conduct (groping, kissing, fondling) committed against another person by force, intimidation, or against a person deprived of reason or under 16 (raised by RA 11648) is punishable by prision correccional. Lasciviousness against children also qualifies under RA 7610.
keywords: lasciviousness, art 336, groping, sexual assault, RA 11648, RA 7610

name: Statutory Rape — Age of Sexual Consent Raised to 16
fullText: RA 11648 raised the age of sexual consent from 12 to 16. Sexual intercourse with anyone below 16 is statutory rape, regardless of consent. Close-in-age exception: relations between persons whose age difference is not more than 3 years (if not abusive) are not criminalized.
keywords: statutory rape, age of consent, RA 11648, 16, close in age

name: Anti-Terrorist Financing
fullText: Prohibits the financing of terrorism, including direct funding and material support. Banks and covered institutions must implement freeze orders from the AMLC.
keywords: terrorist financing, AMLC, RA 10168, freeze order

name: Anti-Smuggling and Customs Modernization
fullText: Smuggling of goods worth ≥ ₱200,000,000 is an economic sabotage offense punishable by reclusion perpetua and a fine of ≥ ₱50,000,000.
keywords: smuggling, customs, CMTA, RA 10863, economic sabotage

name: Anti-Squatting Repealed — Eviction Requirements
fullText: Eviction or demolition of informal settler families requires: 30-day notice; adequate consultation; presence of LGU; execution outside rainy season; relocation site identification. Failure to comply renders the demolition illegal.
keywords: demolition, informal settler, eviction, RA 7279, 30 day notice

name: Air Passenger Bill of Rights
fullText: Passengers delayed > 3 hours due to airline fault are entitled to meals, communication, accommodation if overnight, and rebooking without fee. Cancellation refund must be in cash unless the passenger opts for a travel voucher.
keywords: airline delay, flight cancellation, refund, DTI, passenger rights, DOTC

name: Internet and Mobile Service Quality Standards
fullText: Telcos must achieve at least 80% of advertised speed and uptime. Subscribers experiencing persistent service degradation may file with the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) for refund, rebate, or contract termination without penalty.
keywords: telco, internet speed, NTC, refund, service degradation, mobile data

name: Universal Banking Customer Protection
fullText: Banks and e-money issuers must reverse unauthorized transfers if the customer reports within 15 calendar days and shows no negligence. BSP enforces consumer protection against hidden fees and unfair credit practices.
keywords: BSP, RA 11765, unauthorized transfer, e-money, refund, financial consumer

name: Real Estate Service Act (Brokers / Salespersons)
fullText: Only licensed real estate brokers, salespersons, and appraisers may transact as professionals. Buyers should verify the PRC license number of any agent collecting fees or representing in negotiations.
keywords: real estate broker, PRC, RA 9646, RESA, salesperson, license

name: Truth in Lending Act and Effective Interest Rate Disclosure
fullText: Lenders must disclose total finance charges and the effective interest rate in writing before consummation. Failure exposes lender to twice the finance charge but not more than ₱2,000 plus court costs.
keywords: truth in lending, RA 3765, effective interest rate, disclosure, finance charge

name: Anti-Lapses for Pre-Need / Insurance Products
fullText: Pre-need plan holders enjoy a 30-day grace period and reinstatement rights if lapsed. Insurance Commission supervises and entertains complaints against pre-need and insurance companies.
keywords: pre-need, insurance, lapse, grace period, IC, RA 9829

name: Senior Citizen and PWD Discounts
fullText: Seniors and PWDs are entitled to 20% discount and 12% VAT exemption on medicine, transportation, restaurants, and accommodations. Establishments must provide express lanes and accept the senior/PWD ID issued by the LGU or OSCA.
keywords: senior discount, PWD discount, RA 9994, RA 10754, VAT exempt, express lane

name: Data Breach Notification (72-Hour Rule)
fullText: Personal Information Controllers must notify the National Privacy Commission and affected data subjects within 72 hours of knowledge of a data breach involving sensitive personal information likely to give rise to a real risk of serious harm. Late or no notification is itself a separate offense.
keywords: data breach, 72 hours, NPC, sensitive personal info, notification

name: Rights of Data Subjects
fullText: Data subjects have rights to: be informed, access, object, erase or block, damages, data portability, file complaints, rectification. A formal request to the PIC's Data Protection Officer must be answered within 30 days, otherwise the subject may escalate to the NPC.
keywords: data subject rights, access, erasure, DPO, NPC, 30 days, portability

name: Universal Health Care Act
fullText: Automatic enrollment of every Filipino in PhilHealth (direct or indirect contributor). Benefits include primary care, in-patient care, and outpatient drugs for chronic conditions. Direct contributors are formal-sector workers and self-earning individuals; indirect contributors are subsidized by national/local government.
keywords: universal health care, RA 11223, PhilHealth, automatic enrollment, primary care

name: Mental Health Act
fullText: Recognizes mental health as a basic right; mandates integration of mental health services in primary care; protects against stigma and discrimination. Employers are encouraged to develop mental-health policies; involuntary admission requires court order and second opinion.
keywords: mental health, RA 11036, depression, anxiety, hospital admission, discrimination

name: Generic Medicines Act
fullText: Doctors must prescribe by generic name; pharmacies must offer the generic equivalent. Violations expose health professionals to fines and disciplinary action by the PRC.
keywords: generic medicine, RA 6675, prescription, pharmacy, FDA

name: Reproductive Health (RH) Law
fullText: Guarantees universal access to reproductive health services, including contraception, maternal care, adolescent health, and sex education. Public health facilities must stock contraceptives; conscientious objection allowed for individual providers, not institutions.
keywords: RH Law, contraception, reproductive health, RA 10354, sex education

name: Free Higher Education (UAQTE)
fullText: Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education provides free tuition and fees in state universities and colleges (SUCs) and TESDA programs, plus a Tertiary Education Subsidy for needy students. Available to all qualified students except those who already earned a bachelor's degree.
keywords: free tuition, RA 10931, UAQTE, SUC, TES, scholarship, CHED

name: K-12 Basic Education Curriculum
fullText: Mandates compulsory basic education from Kindergarten through Grade 12 (13 years). Senior High School tracks: Academic, Tech-Voc, Sports, Arts and Design. DepEd implements the curriculum and standards.
keywords: K-12, basic education, senior high, DepEd, RA 10533, curriculum

name: Philippine Mining Act
fullText: Governs the exploration, development, and utilization of mineral resources. Requires Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC), Mineral Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) or Financial or Technical Assistance Agreement (FTAA). Affected indigenous communities have the right to Free Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) under IPRA.
keywords: mining, RA 7942, ECC, MPSA, IP, FPIC, environmental

name: Climate Change Act
fullText: Created the Climate Change Commission. LGUs must integrate climate change adaptation in their development plans. People's Survival Fund finances local adaptation projects.
keywords: climate change, RA 9729, RA 10174, PSF, adaptation, LGU

name: Water Code of the Philippines
fullText: Regulates appropriation, control, conservation, and pollution of water resources. Anyone diverting or appropriating water must secure a water permit from the National Water Resources Board (NWRB).
keywords: water code, PD 1067, NWRB, water permit, appropriation

name: Toxic Substances and Hazardous Wastes Act
fullText: Regulates importation, manufacture, distribution, and disposal of toxic substances. DENR-EMB enforces compliance. Penalties: fines + imprisonment up to 12 years for nuclear waste violations.
keywords: toxic, hazardous waste, RA 6969, DENR, EMB

name: Omnibus Election Code — Election Offenses
fullText: Election offenses include vote-buying, vote-selling, electioneering during prohibited periods, possession of firearms or alcohol within a polling area, and coercion of voters. Penalties: 1-6 years imprisonment, disqualification from public office, and loss of suffrage.
keywords: election, vote buying, BP 881, gun ban, COMELEC, election offense

name: Anti-Political Dynasty / Disqualification
fullText: Constitution prohibits political dynasties as may be defined by law (enabling law remains pending). Election laws disqualify candidates with final criminal conviction involving moral turpitude, dual citizenship, or term-limit violations.
keywords: political dynasty, disqualification, term limit, moral turpitude

name: Dual Citizenship Retention
fullText: Filipino citizens who became naturalized citizens of another country may reacquire Philippine citizenship by taking an oath of allegiance. Re-acquirers retain civil and political rights, including right to vote and own land in the Philippines.
keywords: dual citizenship, RA 9225, reacquisition, oath of allegiance, US citizen

name: Naturalization Process
fullText: Foreigners may seek naturalization via judicial process (CA 473) or administrative process for natural-born qualified aliens (RA 9139). Requirements: 10 years residency (5 with qualifications), good moral character, knowledge of Filipino history, lawful occupation.
keywords: naturalization, CA 473, RA 9139, foreigner, citizenship, residency

name: Income Tax — TRAIN Law Brackets
fullText: Annual taxable income up to ₱250,000 is exempt. Brackets: ₱250k-₱400k = 15%; ₱400k-₱800k = 20%; ₱800k-₱2M = 25%; ₱2M-₱8M = 30%; over ₱8M = 35%. Self-employed and professionals may opt for 8% gross-receipts tax (if gross ≤ ₱3M).
keywords: TRAIN, income tax, BIR, RA 10963, bracket, 8 percent, self employed

name: VAT Threshold and Registration
fullText: Persons with gross sales or receipts exceeding ₱3,000,000 in any 12-month period must register and charge 12% VAT. Below the threshold, businesses are non-VAT and pay 3% percentage tax (1% for 2020-2023 under CREATE).
keywords: VAT, BIR, 3 million, percentage tax, NIRC, sole proprietor

name: Tax Amnesty on Estates
fullText: Heirs of decedents who died on or before May 31, 2022 may avail of estate tax amnesty (6% of net estate, no penalties) until June 14, 2025. Filing is with the BIR Revenue District Office where the decedent was domiciled.
keywords: estate tax amnesty, RA 11569, BIR, heir, succession

name: Donor's Tax
fullText: Donor's tax = 6% of the total gifts in excess of ₱250,000 annual exemption, regardless of relationship between donor and donee. Donations to qualified charitable institutions enjoy full deduction.
keywords: donor tax, 6 percent, NIRC, TRAIN, gift

name: Capital Gains Tax on Real Estate
fullText: Capital gains tax on sale of real property classified as capital asset is 6% of the gross selling price or fair market value (whichever is higher). Filed and paid within 30 days from notarization of the deed of sale.
keywords: capital gains tax, CGT, real estate, 6 percent, 30 days, BIR

name: Quasi-Delicts (Tort Liability)
fullText: Whoever by act or omission causes damage to another, there being fault or negligence, is obliged to pay for the damage done. This forms the basis of tort liability — independent of criminal action. Common applications: vehicular accidents, medical malpractice, employer's vicarious liability.
keywords: quasi-delict, tort, art 2176, negligence, vehicular accident, malpractice, damages

name: Vicarious Liability of Employer
fullText: Employers are liable for the negligent acts of their employees committed in the course of employment. Defense: diligence of a good father of a family in selection and supervision. Common in trucking, BPO transport, and security agency cases.
keywords: vicarious liability, art 2180, employer liability, good father, negligence

name: Damages — Actual, Moral, Exemplary, Nominal, Temperate
fullText: Actual damages compensate proven losses. Moral damages cover physical suffering, mental anguish, social humiliation. Exemplary damages punish gross misconduct. Nominal damages vindicate a right. Temperate damages apply when actual amount cannot be proved with certainty. Each category has independent requirements.
keywords: damages, moral, exemplary, actual, civil code, art 2199, art 2219

name: Succession — Forced Heirs and Legitime
fullText: Legitimate children and descendants share equally in the legitime (1/2 of the estate); the surviving spouse is entitled to a legitime equal to one legitimate child. Illegitimate children get one-half of a legitimate child. A testator may only freely dispose of the disposable portion.
keywords: succession, inheritance, legitime, forced heir, will, testator, civil code

name: Settlement of Estate of Deceased
fullText: If the decedent left no debts and the heirs are all of age (or minors represented by guardians), the estate may be partitioned extrajudicially by public instrument or affidavit of self-adjudication, published in a newspaper of general circulation. Otherwise, judicial settlement is required.
keywords: extrajudicial settlement, estate, Rule 74, self adjudication, inheritance, heirs

name: Notarial Will and Holographic Will
fullText: A notarial will requires the testator and three credible witnesses to sign each page, attested by a notary public. A holographic will is entirely written, dated, and signed by the hand of the testator. Both forms must undergo probate to be valid for transferring property.
keywords: will, notarial will, holographic, probate, testator, succession

name: Civil Code on Contracts — Essential Requisites
fullText: Three essential requisites of a valid contract: (1) consent of the contracting parties, (2) object certain that is the subject matter, (3) cause of the obligation. Defective consent (vitiated by error, force, intimidation, undue influence, or fraud) renders the contract voidable.
keywords: contract, consent, object, cause, vitiated, void, voidable, civil code

name: Action for Reformation of Instrument
fullText: When a written instrument fails to express the true intention of the parties due to mistake, fraud, inequitable conduct, or accident, either party may file an action to reform it. Must be filed within 10 years.
keywords: reformation, contract, civil code, mistake, fraud, 10 years

name: Specific Performance vs Rescission
fullText: In reciprocal obligations (e.g., sale, lease), the injured party may choose between specific performance (compel performance) or rescission (cancel and seek damages). Rescission is automatic only in special cases; in others, judicial action is required.
keywords: specific performance, rescission, art 1191, reciprocal obligation, contract breach

name: Small Claims Court — Updated Threshold
fullText: Small claims jurisdiction now covers money claims up to ₱1,000,000 (excluding interest and costs). Filed at the first-level court of the place of residence of plaintiff or defendant or where the obligation arose. Lawyers are not allowed to appear. Decision on the day of hearing, no appeal.
keywords: small claims, 1 million, A.M. 08-8-7-SC, MTC, MeTC, lawyer prohibited

name: Habeas Data and Writ of Amparo
fullText: Writ of Habeas Data — remedy for any person whose right to privacy is violated through gathering or use of personal data by a public official or private entity. Writ of Amparo — remedy against extralegal killings and enforced disappearances. Both are filed with the RTC, CA, SC, or Sandiganbayan and decided within prescribed periods.
keywords: habeas data, amparo, writ, privacy, extralegal killing, enforced disappearance

name: Forcible Entry vs Unlawful Detainer
fullText: Forcible entry: dispossession by force, intimidation, threat, strategy, or stealth — filed within 1 year from entry. Unlawful detainer: lessor's right to recover after the lease has lapsed or contract was violated — filed within 1 year from demand to vacate. Summary procedure applies; filed at MTC.
keywords: ejectment, forcible entry, unlawful detainer, Rule 70, MTC, 1 year

name: Davao Comprehensive Anti-Discrimination Ordinance
fullText: Prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, age, disability, or socioeconomic status in employment, education, housing, services, and public spaces in Davao City. Penalties: fines up to ₱5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 1 year, plus community service.
keywords: anti discrimination, SOGIE, Davao, ordinance 0417-12, LGBT, equality

name: Davao City Anti-Sagasa Ordinance (Anti-Speeding)
fullText: Penalizes over-speeding within the territorial limits of Davao City. Strictly enforced by the CTTMO. First offense: ₱2,000 fine and 1-month license suspension; second offense: ₱3,500 fine; third offense: ₱5,000 fine and license revocation.
keywords: sagasa, over speeding, Davao, ordinance 0356-13, CTTMO, license suspension

name: Davao City Plastic Ban
fullText: Regulates the use of plastic bags and styrofoam containers by establishments. Wet goods may use plastic only as secondary packaging. Violators face fines and possible permit suspension.
keywords: plastic ban, Davao, ordinance 0361-12, styrofoam, environment

name: Davao City Children's Welfare Code (Anti-Begging)
fullText: Prohibits child begging and child labor in the streets. Children found begging are referred to CSWDO for rescue. Adults using children for begging may be charged under RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking).
keywords: child begging, Davao, CSWDO, trafficking, RA 9208

name: Davao City Women's Development Code
fullText: Establishes the Integrated Gender and Development Division (IGDD) and women-friendly spaces in every barangay. Mandates LGU funding for VAWC desks, women's livelihood programs, and reproductive health programs in coordination with DOH.
keywords: women development code, Davao, IGDD, VAWC desk, reproductive health

name: Davao City Anti-Drug Abuse Council
fullText: Created the City Anti-Drug Abuse Council (CADAC) and barangay-level BADAC. Encourages voluntary surrender, treatment, and rehabilitation programs in partnership with PDEA and DOH.
keywords: CADAC, BADAC, Davao, drug rehabilitation, PDEA

name: Davao City Anti-Loud Music Ordinance
fullText: Prohibits playing of loud music from establishments, vehicles, or residences exceeding allowable decibel levels (typically 50 dB at night). Repeated violations may result in business permit suspension.
keywords: loud music, decibel, Davao, ordinance, noise pollution

name: Davao Region — DENR-XI Environmental Permits
fullText: Establishments in Davao Region engaging in mining, agro-industry, or large-scale construction must secure an Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) from DENR-EMB Region XI. Violations may lead to project stoppage and fines.
keywords: DENR, ECC, Davao, EMB, environmental permit, PD 1586

name: Davao Region — Indigenous Peoples Mandatory Representation
fullText: LGUs in Davao Region must include indigenous people's representatives (Lumad communities) in local councils and seek their Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) before issuing permits in ancestral domains.
keywords: IPRA, RA 8371, Davao, Lumad, FPIC, ancestral domain

name: Davao City Hospital Patient's Bill of Rights
fullText: Patients have rights to informed consent, medical records, second opinion, confidentiality, and refusal of treatment. Hospitals must not refuse emergency care due to inability to pay (RA 10932 — Anti-Hospital Deposit Law).
keywords: patient bill of rights, RA 10932, anti hospital deposit, Davao, emergency

name: Anti-Hospital Deposit Law (Emergency Care)
fullText: Hospitals and medical clinics cannot demand a deposit or any form of advance payment as a prerequisite for confinement or treatment in emergency or serious cases. Violators face ₱100,000-₱1,000,000 fine and 6 months-2 years imprisonment.
keywords: anti hospital deposit, RA 10932, emergency care, refusal, deposit

name: Carnapping with Violence — Special Aggravating
fullText: If during the carnapping the owner, driver, or occupant is killed or raped, the penalty is life imprisonment to death. Mere accomplice or accessory is punished one degree lower.
keywords: carnapping with violence, RA 10883, life imprisonment, killed driver

name: Anti-Violence Against Children in Conflict with the Law
fullText: Children below 15 are absolutely exempt from criminal liability. Children 15-18 are exempt unless they acted with discernment. Detention in regular jails is prohibited; instead, Bahay Pag-asa (DSWD-managed) is used.
keywords: RA 10630, juvenile, discernment, Bahay Pag-asa, DSWD

name: Anti-Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Online (Live Streaming)
fullText: Producing, directing, facilitating, or live-streaming the sexual abuse of a child carries reclusion perpetua and a fine up to ₱5,000,000. ISPs and content platforms must block CSAM URLs reported by the IACAT or PNP-WCPC.
keywords: OSAEC live stream, RA 11930, CSAM, child exploitation, IACAT

name: Anti-Sexual Harassment of Minors in Schools
citation: RA 11648 + DepEd Order 40 s. 2012 (Child Protection Policy)
fullText: Schools must adopt a Child Protection Policy and a Committee on Child Protection. Teachers or school personnel found liable face administrative sanctions plus criminal liability under RA 7610, RA 11648, or RPC.
keywords: school sexual harassment, child protection, RA 11648, DepEd, RA 7610

name: Magna Carta for Workers in the Informal Economy
fullText: Informal workers (sidewalk vendors, kasambahay, ride-hailing riders) gain progressive coverage under SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG through expanded voluntary contributions. DOLE coordinates skill upgrading programs.
keywords: informal worker, magna carta, kasambahay, rider, voluntary contribution

name: Workers' Compensation (Employees' Compensation Program)
citation: PD 626 amending Title II Book IV Labor Code
fullText: Employees injured, contracted illness, or died because of work-related causes are entitled to ECP benefits from SSS (private) or GSIS (government). No-fault principle: gross negligence of the employee may bar claim. Filed within 3 years from cause of action.
keywords: workers compensation, ECP, SSS, GSIS, PD 626, work injury

name: Tort of Abuse of Rights
fullText: Every person must, in the exercise of their rights and in the performance of their duties, act with justice, give everyone their due, and observe honesty and good faith. Abuse of rights may give rise to damages even when the underlying right exists.
keywords: abuse of right, art 19, good faith, damages, civil code

name: Hate Crime (Sex / Gender / Religion / Race)
citation: RPC + Safe Spaces Act + Anti-Discrimination ordinances
fullText: No standalone national hate-crime law yet, but underlying offenses (physical injuries, threats, libel) may be aggravated by motive based on sex, gender identity, religion, or race. Local anti-discrimination ordinances (Davao, QC, Mandaluyong) provide independent penalties.
keywords: hate crime, discrimination, LGBT, religion, motive, aggravating circumstance

name: Service Charge Distribution (Restaurant / Hotel)
fullText: All service charges collected by hotels, restaurants, and similar establishments must be 100% distributed to rank-and-file employees, distributed equally on a payroll period. Excludes managerial employees.
keywords: service charge, RA 11360, restaurant, hotel, tipping, rank and file

name: Acknowledgment of Debt and Prescription
fullText: Actions to enforce a written contract or judgment prescribe in 10 years; quasi-delicts in 4 years. The prescriptive period is interrupted by written extrajudicial demand, written acknowledgment of the debt, or filing of an action.
keywords: prescription, 10 years, civil action, demand letter, interruption

name: Compromise Agreement and Enforcement
fullText: Compromise agreement has the force of res judicata between the parties. Court-approved compromises are enforced by motion; otherwise, a separate action is needed. Must not be contrary to law, morals, good customs, public order, or public policy.
keywords: compromise agreement, settlement, res judicata, civil code, enforcement

name: Easement of Right of Way
fullText: An owner of an enclosed estate (no adequate outlet to public road) may demand a right of way through neighboring estates upon payment of proper indemnity. The route chosen must cause the least damage to the servient estate. Voluntary easements are constituted by agreement; compulsory ones by court order.
keywords: easement, right of way, enclosed land, civil code, art 649, neighbor

name: Action for Quieting of Title
fullText: An owner of real property may bring an action to remove a cloud on the title — e.g., a forged deed, a void contract, an unjust encumbrance. The plaintiff must have legal or equitable title; the action does not prescribe so long as the plaintiff remains in possession.
keywords: quieting title, cloud on title, forged deed, art 476, real property
